quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: J.B. Bickerstaff explains how Elijah stays engaged while not playing
quotes.excerpt: He stays engaged. I can't tell you the amount of conversations that he and I have had.
quotes.quote: He stays engaged. I can't tell you the amount of conversations that he and I have had even when he hasn't been playing. He'll text me, he comes to my office, so he's engaged in what's going on, and that's how you give yourself a chance. quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: J.B. Bickerstaff on the value of the in-season tournament experience
quotes.excerpt: To be able to get an opportunity with this group to continue to do things we haven't done.
quotes.quote: It's great for us. We talked about it beforehand as a group, it's something that we hadn't done before. So to be able to get an opportunity with this group to continue to do things that we haven't done in the past is great for us to give us different experiences, which is really good for us to help us build to where we ultimately want to go.
quotes.social_post: JB Bickerstaff says the in season tournament experience is great for the Pistons group to help them build toward their ultimate goals

structured.context: J.B. Bickerstaff reflects on the value of the in-season tournament experience for his team.

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: J.B. Bickerstaff on the team's collective leadership approach
quotes.excerpt: Our guys are all leaders. We don't just call on one person or two people to lead.
quotes.quote: Our guys are all leaders. We don't just call on one person or two people to lead this team. Everyone on our team has a voice, and when you're in that situation, because guys are out, it doesn't feel like there's a void that has to be filled. It's something that's already natural. So giving guys the power to speak, to use their voice, the guys are understanding who we are and what we're made of and how they hold each other accountable to the standard that we have, it's just not a one-person job.
quotes.social_post: JB Bickerstaff on team leadership: Our guys are all leaders. We do not just call on one person or two people to lead this team. Everyone on our team has a voice

structured.context: J.B. Bickerstaff describes the team's collective approach to leadership.

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: J.B. Bickerstaff on the importance of finding consistent five-man lineups
quotes.excerpt: It comes down to the five-man lineups for us and making sure we're trying to figure out.
quotes.quote: It comes down to the five-man lineups for us and making sure we're trying to figure out who those lineups are consistently. And then on any given night, you got to play the 48 minutes. And to be able to have a guy that you know you can depend on, that can spark the game or change the game the way Paul Reed does, it just gives us the flexibility to be able to do that and use him as a weapon in that way.
quotes.social_post: JB Bickerstaff on Paul Reed: To be able to have a guy that you know you can depend on, that can spark the game or change the game the way Paul Reed does, it just gives us the flexibility to be able to do that

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: J.B. Bickerstaff on tracking in-game scenarios and team performance
quotes.excerpt: We've got guys on the bench that have the capabilities of understanding what the scores are.
quotes.quote: We do. And we've got guys on the bench that have the capabilities of understanding what the scores are. Going into it, we knew where we were as far as Toronto was concerned. We knew the number that we had to be at, but we had people tracking it to see who was where and what and what we needed to do at any given moment.
quotes.social_post: JB Bickerstaff explains that the coaching staff actively tracks in game scenarios and score differentials to know exactly what the team needs to do at any given moment

structured.context: J.B. Bickerstaff explains how the coaching staff tracks in-game scenarios and point differentials against Toronto.

quotes.speaker: J.B. Bickerstaff
quotes.summary_phrase: J.B. Bickerstaff on the benefits of trusting the entire roster
quotes.excerpt: The biggest thing is we have guys here that we trust, and that's the most important thing.
quotes.quote: The biggest thing is we have guys here that we trust, and that's the most important thing is everyone on that roster and in that locker room, we know they can help us be successful. So you're not looking and doubting who you're going to put on the floor. But the only thing that helps you get better is game minutes. It gives individuals an opportunity to get better, which ultimately is going to help your team. But our goal is to be whole at some point. We want to see how good this team can be when we put all our pieces together, and we can still use that depth as a weapon.
quotes.social_post: JB Bickerstaff on the Pistons roster: The biggest thing is we have guys here that we trust. Our goal is to be whole at some point. We want to see how good this team can be when we put all our pieces together
